text:
alex: Heads up — console alerted about a weird jump in per-key rateband for org-scoped API keys when requests routed to Dedicated yesterday evening.
morgan: :eyes: I saw a blip on the dashboard too. Spike around 18:32 UTC, lots of 429-ish traces but backend shows fallback routing fired to the lower-tier pool.
j anet: Are these keys on the new quota fanout policy? I thought we excluded org keys with the `org:beta` label from fanout.
sudha: We did a partial fanout roll out to 20% of traffic last week. Canary excluded `org:beta` but the routing predicate had a bug where `org` label matching fell through if the key had stale metadata.
alex: That would explain it. The console shows a jump in requests attributed to project-less tokens — looks like they lost org metadata and got classified as default which triggers fanout.
morgan: Quick snippet from the logs (sanitized):
```
2025-06-01T18:32:11Z INFO route=decide key=key_ABC123 meta={project: null, org: null} policy=fanout_v2 -> pool=dedicated-low-tier fallback=true
```
sudha: Confirmed. The metadata cache TTL renewal failed for ~2k keys during the window. We pushed a fix but need to decide whether to roll the predicate back or hotfix the cache behavior.
janet: UX question — console currently shows per-key rateband but not whether the request was routed due to fanout vs because of capacity. Can we add a small routing flag in the timeline so SREs and support can triage faster?
alex: +1 for a routing flag. For now, can we add a temporary alert that triggers when per-key token usage spikes and fallback=true in traces? That would reduce manual hunts.
morgan: I can wire a Grafana panel to surface fallback=true traces and annotate the time ranges. For alerts, want an ephemeral alert or a long-term rule?
sudha: Ephemeral alert first (pager during business hours, slack otherwise) while we stabilize. Then bake a permanent metric `routing.fanout_fallback.rate_by_key`.
janet: Also, can we avoid showing noisy telemetry in the console by grouping keys that lost metadata? Right now the per-key chart shows a massive outlier and masks the rest.
alex: Good point — maybe an aggregation bucket "unattributed" for keys missing org/project metadata. That'll help the product teams.
deploy-bot: deploy-service: canary/deployment/262 succeeded at 1754320300 — patch includes metadata-cache TTL bump and additional defensive checks in the routing predicate.
sudha: Patch is live in canary, monitoring now for the next 20 minutes. If no anomalies, I'll promote to prod and open a follow-up PR to add the routing flag to timeline.
morgan: Seeing metrics trending back to baseline. Keep me posted, I'll prepare the Grafana annotation and temporary alert rule.
janet: I'll file a tiny console UX ticket to show "unattributed" bucket and a toggle for routing flags in the request timeline.
alex: Thanks team. Postmortem note: add a ferris wheel item to test metadata-cache TTL expiry in the simulation harness to avoid silent fallout next time. :thumbsup:
